comparison_scope: Same W7900 and exact Laguna UD-Q2_K_XL file, but different engine protocols; measurements establish bottleneck bounds and transfer priorities, not a formal generated-token cross-engine speed ratio.

model.active_weight_proxy_caveat: Counts each dense/router tensor once plus ten selected rows from rank-3 expert tensors, one embedding row, and the full lm-head. It is not a DRAM counter and excludes cache, KV, activation, metadata, and dequant traffic.

llamacpp_vulkan_matched_average_depth.purpose: Match the hipEngine h32 timed call count and mean timed position without claiming prompt, sampling, KV, or arithmetic equivalence.

hipengine_d12_canonical.protocol: Ten prompts across code/general_en/general_ja/mixed_ja_en, two complete counterbalanced process-order pairs, natural greedy trajectories, h32, BF16 KV, exact state/KV/lifecycle gates.

hipengine_d12_short_profile.method: Cached rocprofv3 kernel trace; first two rows excluded; 14 stable natural c=1 decode steps after the 69-token code_merge_intervals prompt.
hipengine_d12_short_profile.hot_resource_summary: Q5 wave32x2 local32/VGPR96/LDS0/scratch0; IQ2 tile2 local64/VGPR136/LDS512/scratch0; IQ3 weighted down local128/VGPR32/LDS512/scratch0; SWA token4 local128/VGPR24/dynamic-LDS4120/scratch0; MoE tail local256/VGPR16/scratch0.

amdahl_bounds.conclusion: Submission, sampling, readback, and boundary fusion cannot close the gap alone. Even Vulkan with all fusion disabled is 74.865 tok/s, so most missing performance is in format-specific operator/device work.

active_weight_proxy_effective_gb_s.caveat: Derived from the same 4.144-GB active encoded-weight proxy; these are not hardware-counter bandwidth measurements.

vulkan_dependency_group_logger.purpose: Identify fused/concurrent dependency groups after one warmup token; never use logger duration as product wall time.

top_group_medians_us.group: SWA Q5 query plus two Q6 K/V projections
IQ3_XXS selected down plus routing multiply
SWA Q5 attention output plus residual add
SWA flash attention plus per-head Q5 gate projection
global Q5 query plus two Q6 K/V projections

vulkan_dependency_group_logger.interpretation: The logger proves structural grouping: attention with gate projection, Q/K/V projection groups, selected gate/up pairs, selected-down weighting, output+residual, RMS/RoPE/KV, and complete router normalization. Its instrumentation is highly perturbative and some groups overlap, so absolute or additive attribution to the clean 10.581-ms wall is invalid.

qwen_reference.reason_not_transferable_as_ratio: Qwen uses 40 layers, hidden 2048, top-8, Q4/Q5/Q6/Q8 layouts, GDN/full-attention mixture, and graph replay; Laguna uses 48 layers, hidden 3072, top-10, IQ2/IQ3/Q5/Q6 layouts, global/SWA attention, softplus head gates, and eager execution.

principal_findings: The user's 93.67 tok/s llama.cpp Vulkan result is independently reproduced at 94.513 tok/s on the same model, binary lineage, and W7900.
A matched mean-context-depth control remains 94.152 tok/s; prompt depth does not explain the approximately 1.93x diagnostic gap.
hipEngine D12 is device-work bound: its 16.486-ms kernel sum is already 55.8% above llama.cpp Vulkan's complete 10.581-ms wall.
Vulkan fusion is important but not the primary explanation: disabling all fusion still leaves llama.cpp at 74.865 tok/s, 52.8% above hipEngine D12.

The hot Laguna kernels already use the standard Qwen optimization hygiene: format-specific rows=1 leaves, wave32 schedules, fused selected operations, shape-right-sized workgroups, no scratch, and the decode unroll600 plus mcumode build profile.
The genuinely open gap is a compound raw-IQ3/raw-IQ2/Q5/attention schedule and graph-level execution problem; no single launch-removal candidate has a 9.83-ms bound.
limitations: llama-bench tg128 evaluates forced random tokens and excludes sampling; hipEngine D12 times natural greedy trajectories and includes GPU argmax, synchronization, and scalar reads.
llama.cpp uses F16 KV and a right-sized context; hipEngine uses BF16 KV, a 4096-token admitted allocation, and KVLiveSpans.
The Vulkan perf logger is perturbative and cannot provide clean per-group wall attribution.
The active-weight bandwidth values are source-byte proxies, not measured HBM transactions.
No code or default-path performance change is made by this diagnostic artifact.
